analysis.title: Nvidia (NVDA): Where Do We Go From Here?
key_insights: Wedbush says NY Times reported on Nov 11 after the close that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang likely had a second relationship with a direct report, per five Nvidia employees. WSJ reports the board is preparing to oust him, and Bloomberg reports the company hired an executive search firm.
Wedbush does not see Huang's ouster as a foregone conclusion but calls it the most likely end game.

An executive transition raises uncertainty for NVDA, but Wedbush argues current valuation and the near-term sales/demand setup moderate the risk. At ~10x FY'28 EPS, almost any level of uncertainty is already priced in.

Wedbush sees no precedent that combines a founding CEO with overarching influence on company direction, the company's importance to tech and tech policy, and no clear succession plan. Uncertainty is therefore higher than in typical CEO transitions.

Precedents cited: Marvell (founder CEO ousted in 2016 after a board investigation into aggressive sales recognition, then prospered under Matt Murphy), HP (Mark Hurd) and Intel (Brian Krzanich) (abrupt exits with no successor, followed by poor periods), and Apple (Steve Jobs, with a clear succession plan and Tim Cook performing well).

Wedbush argues that much of what happens through CY'27 is already set. NVDA has averaged a 5%+ beat over the last 4 quarters, and Wedbush expects another beat and a guidance raise that lifts the 70% revenue growth forecast for next year.

Policy risk: The Information reported on Nov 11 that the US is finalizing a policy blocking Chinese firms from accessing high-end accelerators outside China. Wedbush does not view this revenue bucket as NVDA's largest but expects some sales impact.

Supply chains are tight (material supply locked up through 2027 and in some cases 2028), demand is running ahead of supply (rising GPU rental rates), and Rubin Vera is seemingly near launch. Wedbush expects a prolonged period of solid results regardless of how the executive situation resolves.
NVDA trades at ~10x Wedbush's CY2027 EPS with gross margins around 70% and expected FY1 growth around 70%. Wedbush says semiconductor companies with those metrics typically trade at 20-30x+ P/E.

Wedbush sees four accelerator supply options (NVDA, AMD, Google TPUs, custom silicon), all constrained upstream. Google competes with its main customers, and custom ASICs are hard to build with more failures than successes. Wedbush concludes the industry needs strong third-party accelerator suppliers.

If NVDA stumbles, Wedbush sees AMD (Instinct platform) as the clearest beneficiary and Cerebras as a possible beneficiary, being the only other party with significant traction at large customers. Private firms (Tenstorrent, SambaNova, Etched) would need time to scale.

market_movers.rationale: Wedbush keeps its Outperform rating and $345 price target (~22x FY2028 EPS plus net cash) with the stock at $173.73. It argues a CEO transition adds uncertainty, but valuation at ~10x FY'28 EPS and the demand/supply setup leave room.
Wedbush sees AMD as the clearest likely beneficiary if NVDA stumbles, since its Instinct platform is the most similar solution available today.

sector_views.rationale: Demand for processing is running ahead of supply, with GPU rental rates rising and supply locked up through 2027-2028. Wedbush says the industry needs strong third-party accelerator suppliers.

earnings_insights: NVDA has averaged a 5%+ beat over the last 4 quarters per Wedbush (basis not specified in the note). Wedbush would be surprised if that changes this quarter (upcoming report, not yet printed).
Wedbush expects NVDA to raise guidance and effectively increase the 70% revenue growth forecast for next year (Wedbush forecast, not yet reported).
NVDA trades at ~10x Wedbush's CY2027 EPS estimate (Wedbush estimate), with gross margins around 70% and expected FY1 growth around 70%.
risk_factors: Executive transition at NVDA with no apparent clear succession plan.
Further reporting on the CEO situation and a possible board ouster.
US policy shifts restricting Chinese access to high-end accelerators outside China.

Government regulation weighs on AI growth.
Competitors (AMD, INTC) take share in AI silicon, or customers shift to internally developed products.
NVDA misexecutes on product development or roll-outs.
Possible acquisitions, and weak gaming demand.

Wedbush lists tensions between the West and China, which could cost NVDA share in that market or disrupt its supply chain, as a risk to its price target.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuation at ~10x FY'28 EPS, tight supply, demand ahead of supply, and Rubin Vera near launch give NVDA leeway and a prolonged period of solid results regardless of the executive outcome.
tension_points.bear_case: A founder-CEO exit with no clear succession plan has no close precedent. Wedbush cites Marvell, HP, Intel and Apple as mixed outcomes, and uncertainty rises substantially.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wedbush frames misexecution by NVDA from internal chaos as the trigger for share loss to AMD and Cerebras, but names no specific level or print.
